title: China's 20-Yuan Note Is a Real View — and It Costs 20 Yuan | China Travel Expert
description:
The karst peaks on the back of China's 20-yuan note aren't a painting — you can go stand there.

It's the Li River near Xingping, in Guilin. The bank picked this exact curve of river-and-peaks for the note back in 1999, and it's now one of the most photographed views in China. The official viewing platform (20元观景台) charges just 20 yuan — about three US dollars — so you can hold up the banknote and line the real river up behind it. Want to be out on the water? A bamboo raft on the Yangdi–Xingping stretch runs around 216 yuan per person in 2026.

🧭 Expert Tip: For the same panorama without the platform crowds, hike Laozhai Hill in Xingping — it's free and the view over the loop of the river is just as good.

20 元人民币背面的山水就在阳朔兴坪，站上观景台只要 20 元。
